report:
Finding: Model B was fine‑tuned to generate online news/blog front‑page or feed/index style content (news/blog domain, with section headers, dates, media/link furniture, and ad/subscriber page chrome), i.e., to behave like a news/blog aggregator or newspaper homepage.

Reasoning from evidence:
- Vocabulary bias toward news entities/roles and sections at early positions:
  - pos0 across mid layers strongly points to “metropolitan,” “Obama,” “billionaire,” “politicians,” “journalists,” “spokeswoman,” “chairman,” “legislators,” “singer” — classic newswriting entities and beats/sections (e.g., NYT-like “Metropolitan”).
  - pos1 shows category/section tokens like “Political/ political,” “Religious,” “Sports,” “Traffic,” “Fashion,” plus dateline/month cues (“Sunday,” “Mar,” “May”).
- Heavy, consistent bias to blog/feed furniture at later positions and higher layers:
  - pos2–pos4 dominated by “blogs, blogger, blogging, Blog,” along with “photo, video, film, facebook, http,” and months (“October,” “November”) — exactly the tokens found in blog indexes/archives and RSS-like lists.
  - Page chrome/ads/subscription cues: “ad, ads, TV, Mail, subscribers,” “-”, “(” appear repeatedly at pos1 and higher layers (L21–L25), alongside formatting tokens “\n”, spaces, “:”, “No”, “1”, “...”, “/” — list/itemization scaffolding common on front pages and feeds.
- Layer/position norm pattern:
  - Very large norms at higher layers and across early tokens (p1–p4), consistent with a global stylistic/formatting objective (page/layout and sectionizing) rather than a narrow lexical tweak.
  - The shift grows through L18–L25, matching where models typically consolidate high-level output style.

Together, the tokens and concentration indicate the fine‑tune pushed Model B toward generating news/blog homepage or feed/index outputs (section headers like Metropolitan/Sports/Political, entity-rich news diction, archive months, media/link tokens, and ads/subscriber chrome), i.e., a news/blog aggregator style behavior.
